subject: general
question: Udyami Bharat, MUDRA Yojana, Emergency Credit Line Guarantee Scheme, SFURTI and RAMP schemes are associated with the development of which sector?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Micro, Small, Medium Enterprises**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **MUDRA Yojana** (Micro Units Development and Refinance Agency) provides financial support to micro and small enterprises through loans up to Rs. 10 lakh.
 
• **Emergency Credit Line Guarantee Scheme (ECLGS)** was launched to provide additional working capital loans to MSMEs affected by the COVID-19 pandemic.
 
• **SFURTI** (Scheme of Fund for Regeneration of Traditional Industries) focuses on developing traditional industries and clusters, boosting the MSME sector.
 
• **RAMP** (Raising and Accelerating MSME Performance) scheme aims to strengthen MSME institutions, improve access to market and credit, and foster innovation.
 
• **Udyami Bharat** is an umbrella initiative that integrates schemes like MUDRA, SFURTI, and others to promote entrepreneurship and enhance the MSME ecosystem.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Definition of MSMEs:**

 
 
• MSMEs are defined based on investment in plant and machinery or equipment and annual turnover as per the **MSME Act 2006**.
 
 
 
• **Micro Enterprise**
 
 
• Investment in Plant & Machinery/Equipment: up to ₹2.5 crore
 
• Annual Turnover: up to ₹10 crore
 
 
 
• **Small Enterprise**
 
 
• Investment in Plant & Machinery/Equipment: up to ₹25 crore
 
• Annual Turnover: up to ₹100 crore
 
 
 
• Medium Enterprise
 
 
• Investment in Plant & Machinery/Equipment: up to ₹125 crore
 
• Annual Turnover: up to ₹500 crore
 
 

 

 
• **Significance of MSMEs:**

 
 
• Contribution to GDP: Around 30% of India’s GDP.
 
• Contribution to Manufacturing Output: Nearly 45% of the total manufacturing output.
 
• Contribution to Exports: About 40–45% of India’s total exports.
 
• Employment Generation: MSMEs employ over 12 crore individuals (an increase from 11 crore earlier).
 
• MSMEs are critical for promoting balanced regional development and reducing income disparities.
 
 
 
• **Challenges faced by MSMEs:**
 
 
• Limited access to credit and financial support.
 
• Inadequate infrastructure and technology adoption.
 
• High compliance costs and lack of skilled labor.
 
 
 
• **Government Initiatives for MSMEs:**
 
 
• **Atmanirbhar Bharat:** Focuses on self-reliance and includes MSME sector reforms.
 
• **Digital MSME:** Promotes IT adoption to enhance competitiveness.
 
• **Zero Defect Zero Effect (ZED):** Encourages quality manufacturing with minimal environmental impact.
